newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank Commission presses finmin on Foncier.
newsitem.headline: Bank Commission presses finmin on Foncier.

text.p: French daily La Tribune said on Monday the Banking Commission had pressed the finance ministry to find a solution rapidly for Credit Foncier, a troubled home loans group being allowed to operate despite not meeting normal solvency levels.
The newspaper said the government was hoping to come up with a blueprint in the coming weeks for Credit Foncier but was under pressure from the Banking Commission, which controls banking licences.

Credit Foncier reported losses of 10.6 billion francs for 1995 last April and has since been allowed to continue lending despite sub-standard solvency levels, with its debt market obligations guaranteed by the state.

The finance ministry has had the group taken over by state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations on behalf of the state in the first stage of a plan which involves a partial takeover by cooperatively run Credit Immobilier and a wind-down of the rest.
But amid stiff resistance from unions and politicians, it has appointed a mediator to look into the future of the group.
